note: Inputs of the routing comparison in section 2.1 of the knowledge base. Data, not a script: the harness that reads it is disposable, these rows are not. A model is given a row by running tests/routing.mts against this file.
selection: For each task and each catalogue size n, the catalogue holds the task's own answer plus n-1 distractors drawn from the other 59, and is then ordered, both by a mulberry32 stream seeded from the task id, the size and the salt below. So the correct tool is always present, every point of the sweep has its own catalogue, and no point's prompt is a prefix extension of another's.

collision.note: Inputs of the collision check, not of the sweep above. One catalogue of the six tool files this repository ships, put through the channel the chat routes on: src/chat.mts registers one function per file, carrying the file's own description and the two parameters below, and reads the choice out of message.tool_calls. The two catalogues are the descriptions before and after they were widened to name what apply() performs, and both are put in the same arrangements: position in the catalogue is a variable of its own, so the descriptions are the only thing that differs between the two calls of a pair, and a row is three arrangements rather than one arrangement's luck. A model is given a row by running tests/collision.mts against it.

before.changelog: Draft CHANGELOG.md entries under [Unreleased] from the index, the working tree or free text
before.commit: Split the uncommitted changes into logical commits, each with a Conventional Commits message
before.issue: Draft and create a GitHub issue, picking labels from the repository taxonomy
before.pr: Generate a pull request description from the commits ahead of the default branch
before.release: Cut a release: pick the next version, date the pending changelog section, commit and tag it
before.ship: Commit the working tree and open a pull request

after.changelog: Write entries under [Unreleased] into CHANGELOG.md from the index, the working tree or free text
after.commit: Split the uncommitted changes into logical commits, each with a Conventional Commits message
after.issue: Draft and create a GitHub issue, picking labels from the repository taxonomy
after.pr: Push the branch and create a pull request describing the commits ahead of the default branch
after.release: Cut a release: pick the next version, date the pending changelog section, commit, tag and push it
after.ship: Commit the working tree and open a pull request
